what_the_eye_sees: The face-on view almost works. A flat gold annulus with about 24 radial openings, pointed at the outer end and rounded at the inner end, with small square piercings between their heads. A jeweller who is primed might say "wheel window" from it, but the first read is a daisy or sunflower rosette, or a pierced lattice band. The three-quarter hero does not work. It reads as a ball-bearing cage, a perforated flange washer or a filter ring. The plate is flat with uniform thin bars, square edges and no moulding. The spandrel holes look like rivet or drill holes, not tracery. Nothing says stone, glass or cathedral, and "Gothic cathedral" would not come from either image without a caption.
changes: Give the rails cathedral mouldings instead of a flat plate. Raise the outer rim into a round roll moulding about 0.6 mm proud of the tracery plane, with a stepped second order inside it about 0.3 mm down. Do the same at the inner rail, at about half that scale. Sink the tracery field at least 0.5 mm below both rails so the lights sit in a framed, recessed window. Acceptance: in the 300 px hero the rim shows a lit bead and a shadow step, and the band no longer reads as a stamped washer.

Make the light heads read as tracery, not slots. Change each pointed head to a cusped trefoil head with cusps about 0.3 mm deep at the outer end of each light. Replace the small square spandrel piercings with round oculi or quatrefoils about 1.2 to 1.4 mm across, one between each pair of heads. Acceptance: at 300 px face-on each light shows a visible trefoil and the ring of small openings reads as quatrefoils or roundels, not dots.

Give the bars depth and architecture. Chamfer or round both sides of every radial bar so it reads as a stone colonnette, not a sheet-metal strut, and add a small capital bead about 0.4 mm where each bar meets the inner rail. Consider cutting from 24 to 16 to 18 lights so each light is wider and longer at the same outer radius of 12.4 mm. Acceptance: in the hero the bars catch light along a ridge, and there are few enough lights that each one reads as a single pointed lancet at 300 px.
